texts: Perturb-seq is an experimental approach to map the transcriptional effects of genetic perturbations by combining CRISPR-based genetic screening with information-rich, single-cell RNA-sequencing phenotypes.

Applied at genome-scale, Perturb-seq enables systematic prediction of gene function and in-depth study of complex cellular phenotypes such as aneuploidy, differentiation, RNA processing, and stress-specific regulation of the mitochondrial genome.

This browser includes data from genome-scale Perturb-seq experiments using CRISPRi to target all expressed genes in K562 chronic myeloid leukemia cells and all DepMap essential genes in RPE1 retinal pigment epithelial cells. Use menus at the top of this page to explore data from these studies, including interactive visualizations.
To read more about genome-scale Perturb-seq, see:
Replogle JM, Saunders RA, …, Norman TM, Weissman JS. Cell (2022).
To read more about the development of direct capture Perturb-seq, see:
Replogle JM, …, Weissman JS, Adamson B. Nature Biotechnology (2020).
There are four datasets on SRA:
K562 day 8 Perturb-seq (KD8): targeting all expressed genes at day 8 after transduction
RPE1 day 7 Perturb-seq (RD7): targeting DepMap essential genes at day 7 after transduction
K562 day 6 Perturb-seq (KD6): targeting DepMap essential genes at day 6 after transduction
K562 day 8 Perturb-seq (KD8_ultima): scRNA-seq libraries from the KD8 experiment sequenced on the Ultima sequencing platform rather than the Illumina sequencing platform
In the metadata files, all FASTQ files associated with a single lane/gemgroup of 10X Genomics single-cell RNA-sequencing are listed in a single row.
These files can be used as input for an aligner like celllranger count, starsolo, or kallisto-bustools.
As described in Methods, data were aligned, UMI-collapsed, aggregated, and subset to cells bearing sgRNA(s) targeting a single target gene.
Processed data in the before and after z-normalizion in single-cell and pseudobulk AnnData formats are available.

This link contains commonly requested supplemental data to recreate figures in the paper, including all Anderson-Darling p-values for differential expression analysis, embedding coordinates for Figure 2D, a downloadable interactive scatter plot of Figure 2D, and Z-normalized expression data used to make Figures 2 and 4.
